language.script_notes: Standard Italian as national; German appears bilingually alongside Italian in South Tyrol/Alto Adige near the Austrian border; French appears in Valle d'Aosta.

road_furniture.bollard_color: White with red-diagonal-band front / white back, as national.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Steel W-beam as national; more common on Alpine mountain roads.
road_furniture.curb_style: As national; cobblestone historic centers in Milan/Turin/Venice.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: As national. Autostrada (motorway) signage denser here than the south given the region's industrial road network.

architecture.roof_style: Wooden Alpine chalets with steep, deep-overhang roofs in the mountains; baroque stone architecture in Turin; canal-side Venetian Gothic architecture in Venice.
architecture.roof_material: Terracotta tile in the cities and lowlands; wood shingle/shake in Alpine mountain areas.
architecture.wall_construction: Formal baroque stone facades in Turin; brick and stucco apartment blocks in Milan; colourful stucco canal-side houses in Venice and Burano; timber Alpine chalet construction near the Austrian/Swiss border.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Elegant ochre/cream baroque stone in Turin; brightly painted pastel houses on Burano; muted browns/greens on Alpine timber chalets.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Alpine wooden chalets; Milan's dense apartment blocks and modern skyline; Venice's canal architecture and gondolas; Turin's grand baroque boulevards.

nature.vegetation: Intensively cultivated flat farmland (wheat, corn, rice paddies) fills the Po Valley — almost no original forest remains; coniferous Alpine forest at elevation in the mountains.
nature.terrain: The flat, hazy Po Valley (Italy's industrial and agricultural heartland) is bounded by the dramatic snow-capped Alps to the north and the Apennines to the south; Lake Como/Garda/Maggiore sit at the foot of the Alps.
nature.climate_signature: Humid continental — harsh, foggy winters and hot summers in the Po Valley, a noticeably different feel from the sun-bleached Mediterranean south; frequent haze/fog in valley imagery.

vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: As national; higher density of German-brand cars (BMW, Audi, VW) near the Austrian/Swiss border in the northeast.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Very dense coverage across the industrial/urban Po Valley corridor; good mountain-road coverage in the Alps.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same script, same plate and bollard style
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The north is flatter (Po Valley farmland) with foggy continental winters and Alpine peaks; the south has Mediterranean scrub, olive groves, pastel hill towns and a sun-bleached coastal light the north lacks.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Alpine mountain terrain, wooden chalet architecture near the border, bilingual German signage in South Tyrol
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Italy's red-diagonal bollard and blue-EU-strip plate differ from Austrian/Swiss plates; south of the Alpine border zone, Italian terracotta roofs and cypress trees reappear, which don't occur in Austria/Switzerland.
